subject: Compliance triage: retention windows & temporary BYOK request - MedSpring
messages:
From: Elena Santos <elena.santos@medspring.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedSpring Procurement <procurement@medspring.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance triage - audit logs, retention & KMS exception

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a small pilot but have a few compliance conditions that need to be triaged before procurement signs off. High level asks:

- Retention: we need an evidence-backed proposal for a 90-day trace/event retention for production traffic (audit logs and request metadata).
- BYOK: MedSpring's security team prefers customer-managed keys. For procurement we need a temporary BYOK arrangement while we finalize a longer-term escrow (expectation: ~30 days of keys accessible to us for verification).
- SSO: request that the SSO handshake complete with SCIM provisioning prior to pilot start.
- Evidence pack: a checklist of what you'll provide (sample logs schema, timestamps, redaction controls).

I've attached our evidence request spreadsheet (medspring_evidence_list.xlsx) — it's not all required, but it will help us map gaps. Can you flag which items are auto-generated vs. need product work? Also please call out anything that will likely require an exception or engineering change.

We'd like a short triage call this week if possible. Proposed times: Thu 2pm PT or Fri 10am PT.

Best,
Elena
Elena Santos
Director, Security & Compliance
MedSpring Health

Folks — forwarding MedSpring's asks. Quick summary and proposed triage approach so we can move fast: 

Summary of external asks (from Elena):
- 90-day retention for audit traces/metadata (they want evidence).
- Temporary BYOK arrangement (~30 days) during contract period while escrow is finalized.
- SCIM + SSO provisioning pre-pilot.
- Evidence checklist attached.

Proposed categorization (triage):
1) Product-work (requires roadmap or quick patch): retention window beyond default archive (they need 90d vs our current 30/90 mixed tiers) — determine config and storage cost delta.
2) Security/Controls: BYOK escrow process and short-lived key support — likely needs ops + legal signoff on escrow flow.
3) Identity: SCIM provisioning — should be operational, but we need to confirm SSO metadata handoff timing.

Immediate asks for this thread:
- Grace: can you list the minimum evidence items we can produce in 48 hours (sample log exports, redaction notes, access logs)?
- Priya: feasibility/ETA for a short-lived BYOK path (30 days) and whether we can do key import + temporary grant without major infra work. Also cost/impact of keeping audit traces in hot storage for 90 days.
- Jordan: if we need to offer a one-off exception, what documentation does sales/procurement need (SLA note, runbook, rollback plan)?

I'll try to schedule a 30-minute slot Thu 2pm PT — please flag conflicts. I've exported a short triage note and attached it (triage_notes.md).

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Compliance triage - audit logs, retention & KMS exception (MedSpring)

Thanks for the clear summary Priyom — a few notes from security perspective. I'll keep the reply focused so we can give MedSpring concrete evidence quickly.

What we can ship in 48 hours (low lift):
- Sample audit export for a 7/30/90 day window (CSV + schema) with PII redaction notes.
- Timeline and proof-of-concept for per-tenant audit export (S3 pre-signed export).
- Access logs for the control plane (who accessed keys and when) for the last 30 days.

Open/needs decision (will require engineering or ops):
- 90-day hot retention: storing full, unaggregated traces for 90d will increase storage and indexing costs. Security is OK to support if Sales signs off on cost delta and legal signs an exception for the pilot. Alternative: provide full fidelity for 30 days + compressed/aggregated traces for 60 more days (audit-friendly but more work to query).
- Temporary BYOK (30d): technically possible via KMS key import or a short-term proxy key flow. We need to document the escrow/hand-off process. Roadmap impact: full BYOK lifecycle (rotation, rotation proofs, HSM-backed escrow) is medium priority for infra. We can do a temporary path if procurement signs an operational exception and accepts that keys will be in escrow under a signed process.
- SCIM/SSO: Ops can complete SCIM ahead of pilot; confirm Okta/IdP metadata during the call.

Acceptance criteria we should propose to MedSpring (so Sales has a checklist):
- Evidence pack provided within 48 hours: sample logs, redaction notes, access audit.
- BYOK temporary agreement signed (30d), with escrow runbook attached.
- Pilot start: SSO provisioned + test users added.

I'll draft a short acceptance checklist and the minimal wording for an operational exception (to attach to the procurement doc).

Grace O'Connor
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Compliance triage - audit logs, retention & KMS exception (MedSpring)

Following up with concrete ops feasibility and recommended response to MedSpring. Apologies for the delay — dug into storage and KMS constraints this morning.

Feasibility summary:
- 90-day retention: We can offer two options:
  A) Hot 90d: keep full indexed traces in hot store (queryable) — estimated incremental storage cost ~$1.8k/month for pilot volume (we should present as "cost addendum"). Needs signoff from Sales/Finance.
  B) Hybrid 30/60: full fidelity for first 30d, compressed aggregated traces for next 60d. Query latency for aggregated period will be higher and some fields will be summarized. Lower cost, lower engineering lift.

- Temporary BYOK (30d) flow: implement an import-and-escrow pattern. Steps: customer provides key material -> we import into a dedicated tenant key slot -> generate a signed escrow receipt -> keys are locked after 30d unless contract extended. This requires a short runbook and legal sign-off; engineering impact is small but ops will own the runbook. I attached a simple flow diagram (kms-escrow-flow.pdf) to use as a reference.

- SCIM/SSO: Ops can stand up SCIM provisioning prior to pilot; need IdP metadata from MedSpring by EOD next Tue to meet their timeline.

Recommended reply to MedSpring (short, action-oriented):
1) We can provide an evidence pack in 48 hours (sample logs + access logs + redaction notes).
2) Offer Hybrid retention as default; present Hot 90d as paid addendum.
3) We can do a temporary 30-day BYOK via import-and-escrow with a runbook and receipt; please confirm procurement acceptance and we will prepare paperwork.
4) Request IdP metadata to begin SCIM.

Jordan — can you prepare a minimal procurement addendum template (cost line + operational exception text) so we can attach to the proposal? Priyom — once Jordan has that, please send to Elena and book the call for Thu 2pm PT (or Fri 10am PT if Thu conflicts).

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Staff Product Engineer, Infra & Security, Redwood Inference
